title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not by Grothendieck. It is the first page of a letter from Pierre Deligne to Grothendieck, dated 27 March 1981. 'Schnik' is Grothendieck's nickname, and the letter is signed 'Pierre' on the next page. The previous archive page labels it 'Lettre Deligne sur groupes profinis'. Deligne is answering questions Grothendieck had asked, in the course of his 'Teichmülleries', about the centre and about elements of finite order in profinite completions.

Setting: L is a discrete free group of finite rank and L^ is its profinite completion, the free profinite group.

Deligne's general remarks:
(i) A subgroup of a free group is free, by the topological argument via π1 of a 1-dimensional CW complex.
(ii) Free pro-p groups and free nilpotent groups are well understood (Serre, Cohomologie Galoisienne I.§1.5–1.8, and Lazard).

(a) L^ is torsion-free. Suppose u ∈ L^ has finite order n > 1. Choose an open normal H ⊂ L^ with H ∩ ⟨u⟩ = {e}; the marginal 'mieux' gives this sharper condition.
- Replace L by L' = L ∩ H⟨u⟩. This is a finite-index subgroup, hence free. Its profinite completion is the open subgroup H⟨u⟩, because L^ induces the full profinite topology on finite-index subgroups.
- H⟨u⟩/H ≅ Z/n then gives a surjection φ: L' → Z/n whose generator lifts to the element u of order n in L'^.
- But φ factors through the profinite abelianisation (L'^)^ab ≅ Ẑ^r, which is torsion-free. So the torsion element u maps to 0 and φ(u) = 0, contradicting φ(u) = 1.

(b) L^ has trivial centre (rank ≥ 2). Let u ≠ e be central. Reduce as before to a surjection φ: L' → Z/n with φ(u) ≠ 0, where u remains central in L'^.
- Put K = Ker φ, with closure K^ open in L'^, free profinite of rank r' = n(r−1)+1.
- Look at L'^/(K^,K^)^, an extension of Z/n by K^ab ≅ Ẑ^{r'}. Conjugation by u induces the action of φ(u) ∈ Z/n.
- By the Gaschütz / Chevalley–Weil description, H1 of a Z/n-cover of a wedge of r circles is Z[Z/n]^{r−1} ⊕ Z. So for r ≥ 2 any nontrivial element of Z/n acts nontrivially.
- This contradicts centrality of u.

The next page sketches the analogous statement that open subgroups of Gal(Q̄/Q) have trivial centre, via class field theory. It also reports the Nielsen realisation theorem (Kerckhoff).

The purpose is evident: Grothendieck needed centre-freeness and torsion-freeness of profinite fundamental groups, and of the Galois group, for his anabelian / Teichmüller-tower programme of 1981.
errors: (b) silently needs rank L ≥ 2. For L = Z one has L^ = Ẑ, which is abelian, so the centre is everything. After the reduction, L' has rank ≥ 2 whenever L does, so the argument is fine with this hypothesis.
In (a), the first formulation 'H ne contenant pas u' is insufficient; one needs H ∩ ⟨u⟩ = {e}. Deligne himself corrects this in the margin.
The text writes Zu for ⟨u⟩; since u has finite order, this is the cyclic subgroup it generates (in (b) it becomes Ẑu). This is harmless.
The step 'the completion of L ∩ H⟨u⟩ is H⟨u⟩' uses implicitly that L^ induces the full profinite topology on finite-index subgroups of L. This is standard but unstated.

ideas.what: Free profinite groups are torsion-free, proved by passing to a finite-index subgroup and using the torsion-free abelianisation Ẑ^r
ideas.modern_name: Torsion-freeness of free profinite groups (equivalently, cd = 1 implies torsion-free)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; Serre, Cohomologie Galoisienne (1964); see Ribes–Zalesskii, Fried–Jarden

ideas.what: Free profinite groups of rank ≥ 2 have trivial centre, via the action of a cyclic quotient on the abelianisation of the kernel
ideas.modern_name: Centre-freeness of free profinite groups; Gaschütz / Chevalley–Weil module structure of H1 of a cyclic cover
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard folklore; textbook treatments in Fried–Jarden and Ribes–Zalesskii

ideas.what: Subgroups of free groups are free, via π1 of graphs
(Next page) Open subgroups of G_Q have trivial centre, via class field theory; this is the kind of input later used in anabelian geometry
ideas.modern_name: Centre-freeness of absolute Galois groups of number fields

missed.claim: This is archival evidence that in March 1981 Grothendieck asked Deligne about torsion and centres in profinite completions, at the start of the Teichmüller / anabelian work leading to the Esquisse. Deligne answered with self-contained proofs. It documents Deligne's role as interlocutor in the genesis of the anabelian programme.
missed.quote: et ces deux remarques doivent suffire pour tes questions sur "centre" et "ordre fini"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This matters to historians of anabelian geometry and of the Grothendieck–Deligne correspondence rather than as new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a letter from Deligne with routine, well-known proofs about free profinite groups. Its interest is historical: it documents the questions Grothendieck was asking in 1981.
transcription_corrections: The author is Pierre Deligne, not Grothendieck; 'Cher Schnik' addresses Grothendieck.
'(un [-CW-]complexe de dim 1)' – the image shows 'un CW complexe' with an overwritten first attempt.
'Zu' in the condition H ∩ Zu = {e} means the cyclic subgroup ⟨u⟩. In (b) the image reads 'l'image de Ẑu'.
